title: Supplier Assurance Intake - Rivermark Utilities
summary: Introductory supplier assurance intake to map Rivermark's SIG/CAIQ items to Redwood artifacts. Covered SOC 2 scope, optional ISO 27001 alignment, KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed), SSO and SCIM, audit log exports and log retention, and initial evidence handoff plan. AE to send pricing and evidence index; SE to schedule a deeper KMS/arch diagram session and run a quick log-export sample in customer region.
action_items: Owner: Maya Patel | Item: Share current SOC 2 audit report and Redwood SOC 2 summary; include scoped controls and date | Due: 2026-03-05
Owner: Evan Chen | Item: Prepare KMS integration diagram for VPC/private deployment and list supported HSM/KMS partners | Due: 2026-03-09
Owner: Priya Singh | Item: Provide sample SIG/CAIQ sections most critical to Rivermark (data residency, encryption) so we can pre-map evidence | Due: 2026-03-06
next_steps: Maya to email SOC 2 summary + Redwood security packet
Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive on KMS and audit log exports (Evan + Priya)
Rivermark to flag any controls that must be in-scope for procurement (Liam)
Create a shared evidence folder link and initial mapping spreadsheet
questions: Can Redwood support customer-managed KMS with keys in our AWS account?
What's the max retention for per-tenant audit logs and can logs be exported to S3 in eu-central-1?
How granular is RBAC for model-level access and are there API-level tokens tied to roles?
Do you have an ISO 27001 certificate or roadmap to certify?
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Evan's here from our security/infra team. Who do we have on the Rivermark side?
[00:06] Daniel Ortiz: Hi, Daniel Ortiz, security manager. Thanks.
[00:08] Priya Singh: Priya, cloud architect. Good to meet you all.
[00:10] Liam Walker: Liam, procurement. I'll be mainly tracking process and evidence delivery.
[00:15] Maya Patel: Awesome. Quick agenda — walk through your SIG/CAIQ intake, map to our artifacts, and triage any showstopper items like KMS or data residency. We can also talk SOC 2 and ISO alignment. Sound OK?
[00:25] Daniel Ortiz: Yep. We have an internal supplier assurance packet that hits SIG and a custom form; our security team marked KMS, audit logs, and RBAC as blockers if not satisfied.
[00:32] Evan Chen: Sounds fair. Quick callouts from our side — Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC) modes. For KMS you can choose Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed keys; the latter requires a VPC/private plane and KMS in your cloud account.
[00:44] Priya Singh: When you say customer-managed, do keys live in our KMS and you just use cross-account access? Or do you want us to rotate keys for you?
[00:50] Evan Chen: Good question — we use cross-account KMS grants to decrypt within runtime. Keys remain in your account; Redwood never stores plaintext keys. We can also support HSM partners for FIPS-level requirements but that needs a dedicated/private setup.
[01:05] Daniel Ortiz: And audit logs, are they tenant-separated? We need per-customer logs and the ability to export to our S3 for long-term retention for audits.
[01:12] Evan Chen: Yes, logs are per-tenant and we can stream audit logs to your S3 or a SIEM. Retention defaults 90 days in hosted, but in dedicated/private you can configure longer retention — we can export directly to your bucket in eu-central-1.
[01:25] Liam Walker: Is there an associated cost for the export or long-term storage?
[01:28] Maya Patel: There may be egress/storage costs if we push logs to your bucket but we'll call that out in the pricing appendix; it's typically minimal compared to compute. We'll include a line item.
[01:38] Priya Singh: On RBAC — we need group sync via SCIM. We have strict least-privilege policies; can you do fine-grained roles per model or route?
[01:45] Evan Chen: We support SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning. RBAC can be mapped at the project and route level today; model-scoped roles are in our roadmap but we have API-key scoping for specific endpoints. If you need model-level guards we can surface custom guard rails via policies — it's something we can detail in the technical deep-dive.
[02:05] Daniel Ortiz: How do you handle SOC 2 evidence? We're going to request the report and artifacts — is there an evidence catalog?
[02:11] Maya Patel: Yes, we have a SOC 2 summary pack and an evidence index. We'll share a redacted report and a pick-list that maps SIG questions to our artifacts. Usually we provide: SOC 2 Type II cover letter, control narratives, penetration test summary, and where to find configuration docs.
[02:29] Priya Singh: Do you have ISO 27001 cert yet?
[02:32] Evan Chen: We are not currently ISO 27001 certified; we maintain many controls aligned to ISO and can share our control mapping. Certification is on the roadmap for later this year.
[02:40] Liam Walker: Procurement will want to know acceptable residual risk and SLAs — is there standard language you accept for indemnity/data breach?
[02:46] Maya Patel: Yes — we have a standard enterprise addendum with liability caps, incident reporting timelines, and SLA terms for Dedicated deployments. I'll put our legal template in the shared folder.
[02:55] Daniel Ortiz: On CAIQ, some of the data residency questions are specific — can you confirm where cryptographic keys are stored when using Redwood-managed keys?
[03:03] Evan Chen: If you pick Redwood-managed keys, keys are controlled by Redwood and mirrors are in our cloud provider's region. For region-bound keys the customer-managed KMS route is required.
[03:12] Priya Singh: Ok. For our auditors we need proof that keys never leave our control. That implies customer-managed only.
[03:18] Evan Chen: Yep, that matches our guidance.
[03:22] Maya Patel: We'll mark that in the SIG mapping as 'customer-managed KMS required' for any controls that assert key custody.
[03:30] Priya Singh: Another question — do you provide log signing or WORM storage for audit trails?
[03:35] Evan Chen: We can provision exports to S3 with server-side immutability features (S3 Object Lock) so you get WORM behavior on your side. For hosted shared environments it's not standard, but in private/dedicated we can support it.
[03:48] Daniel Ortiz: Great. For remediation evidence, how long does it take to get screenshots, config exports, or attestation letters?
[03:55] Maya Patel: Typically 3–7 business days for the curated evidence pack; if you need a custom attestation or deeper artifact that might be 7–14 days depending on engineering involvement.
[04:05] Liam Walker: About timelines — procurement needs a 30-day runway from finalizing the security checklist to contract. Can Redwood accommodate that?
[04:13] Maya Patel: Absolutely. We often do a pilot + security sign-off in that window. We'll document a go/no-go milestone in the evidence plan.
[04:20] Priya Singh: Are there any controls that are absolute blockers for Redwood-hosted mode we should know about?
[04:27] Evan Chen: Host mode has limitations around customer key custody and certain WORM/immutable storage guarantees. If those are blockers, we recommend dedicated or private deployment. Also some high-frequency audit exports might require dedicated throughput.
[04:41] Daniel Ortiz: Could you provide a matrix of controls vs artifact (e.g., SIG control -> SOC 2 control -> artifact link)? That's what our team uses to speed reviews.
[04:48] Maya Patel: Yes, we have that and will attach a preliminary map.
[04:52] Priya Singh: One more — network-level egress controls. We need to restrict outbound connections to our VPC endpoints.
[04:58] Evan Chen: Private deployment achieves that; we can allow only your endpoints and block other egress. For hosted we provide private peering options but not total egress lock-down.
[05:10] Liam Walker: Ok sounds good.
[05:12] Maya Patel: Quick recap — we'll send SOC 2 summary + evidence index, Evan will prep KMS architecture and log-export sample, and we'll set up the KMS deep-dive for next week. I'll also include our legal template and a pricing note covering log exports.
[05:26] Daniel Ortiz: We'll send the most critical SIG sections by Friday.
[05:29] Priya Singh: Thanks all.
[05:31] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone — talk soon.
[05:34] (call ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-attribution (Speaker labels are best-effort), short crosstalk, transcription replaced 'KMS' with 'K M S' in a few spots, and timestamps are approximate. Links referenced: Redwood SOC 2 summary (link sent post-call), preliminary SIG mapping spreadsheet (to be shared).
additional_notes: Customer emphasized customer-managed KMS + S3 export in eu-central-1 as procurement blockers. Suggested timeline: pilot in 30 days; legal template requested. Redacted SOC 2 and evidence index to be shared.
